Abstract excerpt: Large video-language models (LVLMs) have shown remarkable performance on multimodal tasks like multimodal emotion recognition (ER) in the wild. ER is inherently multimodal, requiring a joint understanding of facial expressions, vocalizations, language, biosignals, and gestures. However, real-world deployment remains challenging: modalities may be missing or noisy at test time. Partial observations can be viewed as a distribution shift relative to the complete-modality distribution.
